players.product: Suisi cloud AI chips (DSA architecture; Suisi 320 / Suisi 400) on S60 inference cards and L600 training-inference OAM modules, CloudBlazer POD compute systems and 10,000-card clusters with the TopsRider software stack

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus, business: Enflame (Shanghai Enflame Technology, founded 2018) is a fabless cloud AI chip company. It has developed four architecture generations and 5 cloud AI chips on its own instruction set, with its GCU-CARE compute unit and GCU-LARE chip-to-chip interconnect (positioned against NVIDIA TensorCore and NVLink), and its own TopsRider software stack instead of CUDA. Products: AI accelerator cards and OAM modules (one cloud AI chip per card), CloudBlazer POD compute systems (4-8 AI servers per rack, typically 32 to 64 cards per POD) and multi-rack clusters. 313 domestic invention patents at end-2025.
quarterly_data.figure: 4 architecture generations, 5 cloud AI chips; 313 invention patents

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus, chip generations: Suisi 1.0 (2019; T1x training and i1x inference cards), Suisi 2.0 (2021; T2x training, 300W), Suisi 2.5 (2021; i2x inference, 150W), Suisi 320 (2024, 3rd-gen architecture; S60 inference card, 300W) and Suisi 400 (2025, 4th gen; FP8; L600 training-inference OAM module, 700W, up to 128-card full interconnect, clusters of 10,000 cards and more). At the prospectus date the L600 had come back from the fab but was not yet in large-scale volume delivery; over 80% of card / module revenue in the reporting period came from inference products.
quarterly_data.figure: Suisi 400 / L600 700W OAM, up to 128-card interconnect; inference >80% of card revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus, revenue: operating revenue RMB 10 thousand 30,118.74 (2023), 72,238.74 (2024) and 99,016.00 (2025), a 81.32% compound growth rate. 2025 main-business revenue 98,630.11: AI accelerator cards and modules 85,642.40 (86.83%), compute systems and clusters 12,823.51 (13.00%), IP licensing and other 164.20. Main-business revenue was 99.99% from mainland China in 2025. Net loss RMB 10 thousand -116,388.10 in 2025 (-151,031.58 in 2024).

Prospectus, cards and margins: 2025 production 74,159 and sales 66,330 accelerator cards / modules (49,422 and 38,045 in 2024); card / module revenue up 178.46% on 64,890 units (+197.81%) at an average price of RMB 13,198.09 per card (-6.50%). The company attributes 2024 growth to the volume launch of its 3rd-generation card and 2025 growth to that card ramping in internet customers' AI workloads. Main-business gross margin 31.78% in 2025 (cards 32.71%, systems and clusters 25.71%) vs 30.59% in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: 66,330 cards sold (2025); ASP RMB 13,198.09; gross margin 31.78%

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus: Chengdu Hi-Tech Electronics (Chengdu Gaoxin Vision Electronic Information Technology Service) took RMB 10 thousand 14,511.63 of compute systems and clusters in 2025, 14.15% of revenue; it is the only customer to which Enflame delivered a full cluster as general integrator (a 2022 contract of RMB 10 thousand 18,012.52 for the Chengdu domestic AI video infrastructure platform cluster, accepted in 2025).

Prospectus, suppliers: Shennan Circuits supplied board processing (accelerator card manufacturing) worth RMB 10 thousand 9,597.28 in 2025, 10.32% of purchases (5,914.79 in 2024); Enflame hands finished chips to board makers, which supply the carrier board, power / signal management and thermal parts.
Prospectus, suppliers: Tiantong Jingdian New Technology (a Tiantong Holdings subsidiary) supplied board processing worth RMB 10 thousand 6,523.09 in 2025, 7.01% of purchases.

Prospectus: Shanghai Shanmu Electronics supplied servers and supporting hardware under a 2024 contract of RMB 10 thousand 11,296.40 (completed); servers are bought in Buy&Sell mode for Enflame's compute-system and cluster deliveries.

Prospectus: Tencent Cloud (a related party) sold Enflame servers for accelerator-card adaptation R&D (RMB 10 thousand 1,617.74 in 2025) and cloud services (RMB 10 thousand 252.85 in 2025); in 2024 it supplied a cloud compute software platform and operations service for a compute-center project.

Prospectus: Suzhou TF-AMD Semiconductor (Tongfu Chaowei, a subsidiary of Tongfu Microelectronics) and Unis Digital (Suzhou) (a Unisplendour subsidiary) are named among Enflame's suppliers; year-end payables to TF-AMD were RMB 10 thousand 185.82 (2023) and to Unis Digital (Suzhou) 6,964.07 (2024). The prospectus does not state what each supplied.

Prospectus, supply: the company is fabless; wafers are made by a foundry and packaged and tested by OSATs (none named). Because wafer makers and memory IDMs are concentrated, it orders wafers and memory chips ahead and pays large prepayments; prepayments were RMB 10 thousand 38,813.22 at end-2025. 2025 purchases RMB 10 thousand 93,018.69: direct materials (wafers, memory chips) 52.21%, board processing 17.53%, packaging and test 10.09%. In 2024 it impaired a prepayment of RMB 10 thousand 1,938.88 because a supplier could not deliver due to international trade friction. Its 2026 neutral-case card / module gross margin is below any reporting-period year because of tight wafer capacity and rising memory prices.
quarterly_data.figure: Prepayments RMB 10 thousand 38,813.22; direct materials 52.21% of purchases

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus, recent results and company forecast: H1 2026 revenue RMB 10 thousand 112,030.76, up 279.08% (Q2 2026 83,331.43, up 200.50%); H1 pre-tax loss RMB 10 thousand -63,237.11. The company forecasts January-September 2026 revenue of RMB 10 thousand 230,000.00 to 300,000.00 (up 325.78% to 455.36%) and a net loss of -86,000.00 to -70,000.00; it expects consolidated profit in 2026 or 2027 (roughly break-even in 2026 in its neutral case), with 2026 delivery types, volumes and prices already set in orders on hand at end-February 2026.

Prospectus: the company says it has kept R&D spending above RMB 1 billion a year (stated as over 10 hundred million yuan), and puts its 2025 share of China's AI accelerator market at about 1.7% by unit volume (IDC data and its own sales volume). Its Qingyang (Gansu) 10,000-card cluster is the first domestic 10,000-card inference cluster rated five stars by CAICT; it also took part in building compute centers in Wuxi (Jiangsu).

Prospectus: the top-5 customers took 96.89% of 2025 revenue (92.60% in 2024, 96.50% in 2023); the company attributes the concentration to large single contracts in its compute-system and cluster business and to large-scale deployment in internet customers' AI workloads.
